14	// This test verifies that there is no memory leak when handling TLS certificate errors.
15	// It simulates the error by using a server with a self-signed certificate.
16	test('no memory leak with TLS certificate errors', { timeout: 20000 }, async (t) => {
17	  if (!hasGC) {
18	    throw new Error('gc is not available. Run with \'--expose-gc\'.')
19	  }
20	
21	  const { ok } = tspl(t, { plan: 1 })

23	  // Create HTTPS server with self-signed certificate

25	    key: fs.readFileSync(path.join(__dirname, 'fixtures', 'key.pem')),
26	    cert: fs.readFileSync(path.join(__dirname, 'fixtures', 'cert.pem')),
27	    joinDuplicateHeaders: true
28	  }
29	
30	  // Create a server that always responds with a simple message
31	  const server = https.createServer(serverOptions, (req, res) => {
32	    res.writeHead(200)
33	    res.end('test response')
34	  })
35	
36	  // Start server on a random port
37	  await new Promise(resolve => server.listen(0, resolve))
38	  const serverUrl = `https://localhost:${server.address().port}`
39	
40	  t.after(closeServerAsPromise(server))
41	
42	  // Function to make a request that will trigger a certificate error
43	  async function makeRequest (i) {
44	    try {
45	      // The request will fail with UNABLE_TO_VERIFY_LEAF_SIGNATURE or similar
46	      // because we're using a self-signed certificate and not telling
47	      // Node.js to accept it.
48	      //
49	      // Do not add an AbortSignal timeout here: the test timeout already
50	      // protects against hangs, and per-request timeout signals retain enough
51	      // short-lived objects to make this memory regression test flaky.
52	      const res = await fetch(`${serverUrl}/request-${i}`)
53	      const text = await res.text()
54	      return { status: res.status, text }
55	    } catch (e) {
56	      // In real code, without the fix, this would leak memory
57	      if (e?.cause?.code === 'CERT_SIGNATURE_FAILURE' ||
58	          e?.cause?.code === 'DEPTH_ZERO_SELF_SIGNED_CERT' ||
59	          e?.cause?.code === 'ERR_TLS_CERT_ALTNAME_INVALID' ||
60	          e?.cause?.code === 'UNABLE_TO_VERIFY_LEAF_SIGNATURE') {
61	        return { status: 524, text: 'Certificate Error' }
62	      }
63	      // Return for any other error to avoid test interruption
64	      return { status: 500, text: e.message }
65	    }
66	  }
67	
68	  // Counter for completed requests
69	  let complete = 0
70	  const requestCount = 400
71	
72	  // Track memory usage

74	  let baselineMemory = 0

93	      global.gc()
94

96	
97	      // Establish baseline after first batch

99	        baselineMemory = memUsage.heapUsed
100	      }
101	
102	      measurements.push({
103	        complete,
104	        heapUsed: memUsage.heapUsed
105	      })
106	
107	      console.log(`Completed ${complete}/${requestCount}: Heap: ${Math.round(memUsage.heapUsed / 1024 / 1024)}MB`)
108	
109	      // Check memory trend after we have enough data
110	      if (measurements.length >= 4) {
111	        const hasLeak = checkMemoryTrend()
112	        if (hasLeak) {
113	          return true // Indicates a leak was detected
114	        }
115	      }
116	    }
117	
118	    return false // No leak detected
119	  }

121	  // Main test logic
122	  async function runTest () {
123	    const batchSize = 50
124	
125	    for (let i = 0; i < requestCount; i += batchSize) {
126	      const leakDetected = await processBatch(i, batchSize)
127	      if (leakDetected) {
128	        // If a leak is detected, fail the test
129	        assert.fail('Memory leak detected: heap usage is consistently increasing at a significant rate')
130	        return
131	      }
132	
133	      // Check if we have sufficient measurements or have done 350 requests
134	      if (measurements.length >= 7 || complete >= 350) {
135	        break
136	      }
137	    }
138	
139	    // Final check
140	    const finalCheckResult = finalMemoryCheck()
141	    if (finalCheckResult) {
142	      assert.fail(`Memory leak detected: ${finalCheckResult}`)
143	    } else {
144	      ok(true, 'Memory usage has stabilized')
145	    }
146	  }
147	
148	  // Check if memory usage has a concerning trend
149	  function checkMemoryTrend () {
150	    // Calculate memory growth between each measurement
151	    const growthRates = []
152	    for (let i = 1; i < measurements.length; i++) {
153	      const prev = measurements[i - 1].heapUsed
154	      const current = measurements[i].heapUsed
155	      growthRates.push((current - prev) / prev)
156	    }
157	
158	    // Calculate growth from baseline
159	    const totalGrowthFromBaseline = (measurements[measurements.length - 1].heapUsed - baselineMemory) / baselineMemory
160	
161	    // Calculate average growth rate
162	    const avgGrowthRate = growthRates.reduce((sum, rate) => sum + rate, 0) / growthRates.length
163	
164	    console.log(`Growth from baseline: ${(totalGrowthFromBaseline * 100).toFixed(2)}%`)
165	    console.log(`Average growth rate: ${(avgGrowthRate * 100).toFixed(2)}%`)
166	    console.log(`Growth rates: ${growthRates.map(r => (r * 100).toFixed(2) + '%').join(', ')}`)
167	
168	    // Only flag as leak if all conditions are met:
169	    // 1. Consistent growth (majority of measurements show growth)
170	    // 2. Average growth rate is significant (>2%)
171	    // 3. Total growth from baseline is significant (>20%)
172	
173	    // Count how many positive growth rates we have
174	    const positiveGrowthRates = growthRates.filter(rate => rate > 0.01).length
175	
176	    return (
177	      positiveGrowthRates >= Math.ceil(growthRates.length * 0.75) && // 75% of measurements show growth >1%
178	      avgGrowthRate > 0.02 && // Average growth >2%

180	    )
181	  }
182

186

189	    console.log(`Final growth from baseline: ${(totalGrowthFromBaseline * 100).toFixed(2)}%`)
190	
191	    // Calculate final slope over the last 150 requests
192	    const lastMeasurements = measurements.slice(-3)
193	    const finalSlope = (lastMeasurements[2].heapUsed - lastMeasurements[0].heapUsed) /
194	                      (lastMeasurements[2].complete - lastMeasurements[0].complete)
195	
196	    console.log(`Final memory slope: ${finalSlope.toFixed(2)} bytes per request`)

198	    // Only consider it a leak if:

200	    if (totalGrowthFromBaseline > 0.25) {
201	      return `Excessive memory growth of ${(totalGrowthFromBaseline * 100).toFixed(2)}%`
202	    }
203	
204	    // 2. Memory is still growing rapidly at the end (>2000 bytes per request)
205	    if (finalSlope > 2000) {
206	      return `Memory still growing rapidly at ${finalSlope.toFixed(2)} bytes per request`
207	    }

209	    return false

content.text:
Fixed in `lib/dispatcher/client.js:570-580`.

**Change:** replaced `assert(client[kRunning] === 0)` in the `ERR_TLS_CERT_ALTNAME_INVALID` branch of `handleConnectError` with a drain loop that errors in-flight running requests (advancing `kRunningIdx` and nulling the queue slots, as `onError`/the socket-error paths do), then resyncs `kPendingIdx` before the existing servername-filtered pending drain.

**Verified against a live repro** (temporary script, since removed): HTTPS server using `test/fixtures/{key,cert}.pem`, a `Pool` with `pipelining: 10, connections: 2` and `connect: { ca: ca.pem, servername: 'definitely-not-localhost.example.com' }`, 20 concurrent requests. With a probe inserted in the new loop, `kRunning` was 1 on eleven separate connect errors — i.e. the old assertion's premise is genuinely violated in practice, not just theoretically. All 20 requests now reject with `ERR_TLS_CERT_ALTNAME_INVALID` and the process does not crash.

**Tests:** `test/client-errors.js`, `test/client-connect.js`, `test/pool.js`, `test/client-pipelining.js`, `test/connect.js`, `test/client-request.js` — 101 pass, 0 fail. `test/tls-cert-leak.js` passes (needs `--expose-gc`; it throws otherwise, unrelated to this change). I could not run `npx standard` — the command was denied — but the added code follows the file's existing style and `assert` is still used elsewhere in the file, so its import is not orphaned.

**Co-change partner** (`lib/dispatcher/client-h2.js`, 35% co-change per COMPLEX.md): opened it; **no change needed**. Its two `assert(err.code !== 'ERR_TLS_CERT_ALTNAME_INVALID')` lines (`client-h2.js:380`, `:521`, plus `client-h1.js:922`) sit on session/socket error handlers that only run once an HTTP context exists, whereas this bug is on the connect path before that — those asserts document that the altname error cannot arrive there, and they still hold.

Nothing committed.
